B013-01.notes: Multiply by conjugate (2+3i): (10+15i+2i+3i^2)/13 = (7+17i)/13. B forgets i^2=-1; C uses 4-9 in denominator.

flags: minor: answer choices can be tested directly (only 36 reverses to a number 27 larger with digit sum 9), so this plays as easy
B013-03.notes: b-a=3, a+b=9 so a=3, b=6; 63-36=27. D (63) is the reversed number.

B013-05.notes: x=1 gives f(2)=5, so y=-5+1=-4. Point (1,-4). A doubles x; B ignores the reflection; C negates after adding 1.

B013-06.notes: Vector from center (2,-3); 90 deg CCW gives (3,2); add (1,1) to get (4,3). C is the rotated vector without translating back. Borderline medium/hard because of the non-origin center.

flags: minor: other quartile conventions (e.g., linear interpolation) give 9.75, which is not a choice, so the standard median-of-halves answer is the only defensible one

B013-09.notes: (40-2w)(25-2w)=544 gives 4w^2-130w+456=0, so w=4 or 28.5 (28.5 is extraneous because it makes the dimensions negative). Check: 32*17=544. C is the 1w mistake.

B013-10.notes: 0.8(1+p)=1 gives p=0.25. 20% is the classic trap.
